subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make 1024 the default Docker sandbox PID limit, and what explicit opt-out or migration contract should accompany that security default?
rationale: The code change is small, but it changes a security-sensitive default for existing installations and the current public schema does not expose Docker's unlimited sentinel.

options.title: Adopt with opt-out
options.body: Keep the secure default only after adding schema/docs/tests for an explicit Docker-default or unlimited opt-out and showing real Docker proof.

options.title: Keep explicit-only config
options.body: Do not change the runtime default yet; document or audit-warning the risk until maintainers choose a broader resource-limit policy.

options.title: Accept hard cap
options.body: Merge the 1024 default as an intentional breaking hardening change and own any workload compatibility fallout in release notes/support.

recommendation.title: Adopt with opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default only after adding schema/docs/tests for an explicit Docker-default or unlimited opt-out and showing real Docker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox hardening and current-line history make this the best available routing owner for the default-policy choice.
